dataset: Codex Conditions official eye etiology B31
policy: Fill only currently absent bilingual etiology fields for five eye Conditions. Preserve existing narrative, red flags, treatment scope, relations, and provenance; append two direct NIH/NLM or NHS sources per record. Distinguish mechanisms, risk factors, look-alike diagnoses, and urgent complication pathways without converting association into causation.

cond.vitreous_floaters.etiology_zh: 玻璃體飛蚊是光線穿過玻璃體內的纖維束、細胞或凝聚物時，其陰影投射在 retina 上所產生的視覺現象，不是物體真的漂在眼前。最常見機制是年齡相關 vitreous syneresis：原本透明的膠狀玻璃體液化、收縮並形成可見凝聚物；若玻璃體自 retina 分離，則稱 posterior vitreous detachment（PVD），常伴新發 flashes。近視、白內障手術、眼內發炎、眼外傷及糖尿病相關 vitreous hemorrhage 可增加或造成 floaters，但慢性穩定飛蚊不等同 retinal disease。少數急性新發病例源自 retinal tear、retinal detachment、眼內出血或 uveitis。突然大量新飛蚊、閃光、視野幕簾／陰影或視力下降不是單純老化的安全表現，須即時散瞳眼底檢查，以免漏掉可致永久視力損失的 retinal tear 或 detachment。
cond.vitreous_floaters.etiology_en: Vitreous floaters are visual phenomena created when strands, cells, or condensations within the vitreous cast shadows on the retina; objects are not literally floating in front of the eye. The commonest mechanism is age-related vitreous syneresis, in which the normally clear gel liquefies, contracts, and forms visible clumps. Separation of vitreous from retina is posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) and often accompanies new flashes. Myopia, cataract surgery, intraocular inflammation, eye injury, and diabetes-related vitreous hemorrhage can predispose to or cause floaters, but chronic stable floaters are not synonymous with retinal disease. A minority of acute presentations result from retinal tear or detachment, intraocular bleeding, or uveitis. A sudden shower of new floaters, flashes, a curtain or shadow in the field, or reduced vision is not a safely attributable aging change and requires prompt dilated retinal examination to avoid missing a sight-threatening tear or detachment.

cond.ocular_hypertension.etiology_zh: 眼壓過高症（ocular hypertension）指 intraocular pressure 高於預期範圍，但尚未證實 glaucomatous optic-nerve damage 或相應 visual-field loss；它是風險狀態，不等同 glaucoma。眼壓取決於 ciliary body 產生 aqueous humor 與 trabecular／uveoscleral outflow 的平衡；多數情況是房水排出阻力增加，而非製造過多。眼壓讀值亦受 corneal thickness、量測方法與日內波動影響，所以單次高值不能獨立確診。年齡、家族史、較高基線眼壓、薄 central cornea、近視，以及 African／Hispanic ancestry 與日後 primary open-angle glaucoma 風險相關；steroid exposure、uveitis、眼外傷、色素或 pseudoexfoliative material、眼內手術可造成 secondary elevation。並非每位高眼壓者都會發展 glaucoma，而 normal-pressure glaucoma 亦可在正常讀值下發生。急性劇烈眼痛、紅眼、虹視、頭痛、噁心或視力驟降提示 acute angle closure 等急症，不是普通無症狀 ocular hypertension。
cond.ocular_hypertension.etiology_en: Ocular hypertension means intraocular pressure above the expected range without established glaucomatous optic-nerve damage or corresponding visual-field loss. It is a risk state, not glaucoma itself. Pressure reflects the balance between aqueous humor production by the ciliary body and trabecular or uveoscleral outflow; increased resistance to drainage, rather than overproduction, is the usual pathway. Corneal thickness, measurement technique, and diurnal variation also affect the reading, so one elevated measurement is insufficient by itself. Older age, family history, higher baseline pressure, a thin central cornea, myopia, and African or Hispanic ancestry are associated with later primary open-angle glaucoma risk. Steroid exposure, uveitis, eye trauma, pigment or pseudoexfoliative material, and intraocular surgery can cause secondary elevation. Not everyone with high pressure develops glaucoma, and normal-tension glaucoma can occur despite readings in the conventional range. Severe acute eye pain, red eye, halos, headache, nausea, or abrupt visual loss suggests an emergency such as acute angle closure rather than routine asymptomatic ocular hypertension.

cond.amblyopia.etiology_zh: 弱視是視覺發育敏感期內，一眼（少數為雙眼）提供持續較差或互相衝突的影像，使 brain 逐漸抑制該眼訊號而形成的 developmental visual-processing disorder；它不是眼肌「懶惰」，外觀也可完全正常。主要路徑包括 strabismic amblyopia（雙眼未對位而抑制偏斜眼）、anisometropic／refractive amblyopia（兩眼屈光差異或未矯正的高屈光不正造成一眼影像長期模糊），以及 deprivation amblyopia（congenital cataract、ptosis 或其他 optical-axis obstruction 阻斷清晰影像）。早產、低出生體重、發展障礙及兒童白內障／弱視家族史增加風險，但不是每名高風險兒童都會發病。弱視與 strabismus 不是同義詞：斜視可造成弱視，弱視也可不伴肉眼可見斜視。由於兒童常不自覺單眼視力差，需靠篩檢發現；嬰幼兒瞳孔白色反光、明顯下垂遮瞳或新發眼位偏斜須優先排除 cataract、retinoblastoma 等阻斷或威脅視力的病因。
cond.amblyopia.etiology_en: Amblyopia is a developmental visual-processing disorder in which persistently degraded or conflicting input from one eye, less often both eyes, during the sensitive period leads the brain to suppress that signal. It is not a “lazy” eye muscle, and the eye may appear structurally normal. Major pathways are strabismic amblyopia, in which misalignment leads to suppression of the deviating eye; anisometropic or refractive amblyopia, in which unequal or high uncorrected refractive error leaves one retinal image chronically blurred; and deprivation amblyopia, in which congenital cataract, ptosis, or another optical-axis obstruction prevents a clear image. Prematurity, low birth weight, developmental disability, and family history of childhood cataract or amblyopia increase risk but are not individually diagnostic. Amblyopia and strabismus are not synonyms: strabismus can cause amblyopia, while amblyopia can occur without visible deviation. Because children may not notice unilateral loss, screening is essential. A white pupillary reflex, ptosis covering the pupil, or new ocular deviation in an infant or child requires priority assessment for cataract, retinoblastoma, or another vision-threatening obstructive cause.

cond.strabismus.etiology_zh: 斜視是兩眼視軸不能同時對準同一目標，可呈 esotropia、exotropia、hypertropia 或 hypotropia；核心問題是 binocular motor alignment 與感覺融合失衡，不應簡化為某一條眼肌「太弱」。兒童型可與遺傳易感、未矯正 hyperopia 引起的過度 accommodative convergence、先天神經發育差異、早產或視力不對稱相關，且不少病例無單一可辨原因；持續偏斜會令發育中的 brain 抑制一眼，繼而造成 amblyopia。成人新發斜視常屬 acquired disease，可由 cranial-nerve palsy、stroke、diabetes、thyroid eye disease、myasthenia gravis、orbital disease、外傷或一眼視力喪失破壞融合而起。嬰兒寬鼻樑造成的 pseudostrabismus 不是真正眼位偏斜，但僅靠外觀不能可靠排除真斜視。兒童固定新發偏斜、白瞳、視力下降或神經症狀，以及成人突然 binocular diplopia、眼瞼下垂、瞳孔異常、劇烈頭痛或肢體症狀，須緊急評估其眼內、眶內或神經病因。
cond.strabismus.etiology_en: Strabismus is failure of both visual axes to align simultaneously on the same target and may be esotropia, exotropia, hypertropia, or hypotropia. The central problem is disturbed binocular motor alignment and sensory fusion, not simply one “weak” eye muscle. Childhood disease can relate to inherited susceptibility, excessive accommodative convergence from uncorrected hyperopia, congenital neurodevelopmental differences, prematurity, or asymmetric vision, although many cases have no single identifiable cause. Persistent deviation can make the developing brain suppress one eye and cause amblyopia. New adult strabismus is often acquired and may follow cranial-nerve palsy, stroke, diabetes, thyroid eye disease, myasthenia gravis, orbital disease, trauma, or loss of vision in one eye that disrupts fusion. A broad nasal bridge can create pseudostrabismus in infants, but appearance alone cannot reliably exclude true deviation. A fixed new deviation, leukocoria, visual loss, or neurologic findings in a child, and sudden binocular diplopia with ptosis, pupil abnormality, severe headache, or limb symptoms in an adult require urgent assessment for ocular, orbital, or neurologic disease.

cond.dacryocystitis.etiology_zh: 淚囊炎是 nasolacrimal drainage obstruction 使淚液滯留於 lacrimal sac，繼而發生的感染性發炎；阻塞是底層機制，細菌在停滯淚液內增殖是急性發炎的近端原因。嬰兒多因 distal nasolacrimal duct 的先天膜性阻塞或發育未完全；成人 acquired obstruction 常與年齡相關狹窄、慢性鼻腔／鼻竇發炎、外傷、手術或較少見的結石、腫瘤相關。急性病例通常為單側內眥下方疼痛、紅腫與膿性 reflux；慢性阻塞則可主要表現為 epiphora、反覆分泌物或較輕微腫脹。單純流淚不等同淚囊炎，亦可來自 ocular-surface irritation、過敏、眼瞼位置異常或淚液產生過多；只有感染性淚囊發炎才符合本病。紅腫向 eyelid／orbit 擴展、眼球突出、眼球活動疼痛或受限、視力下降、發燒或全身中毒表現提示 preseptal／orbital cellulitis、abscess 或 sepsis，須緊急處理，而不是以局部輔助療法延誤抗感染與引流評估。
cond.dacryocystitis.etiology_en: Dacryocystitis is infectious inflammation that develops when nasolacrimal drainage obstruction causes tears to stagnate in the lacrimal sac and bacteria proliferate. Obstruction is the underlying mechanism, while secondary microbial growth is the proximate cause of acute inflammation. In infants, the usual pathway is a congenital distal-duct membrane or incomplete duct development. Acquired adult obstruction commonly reflects age-related narrowing, chronic nasal or sinus inflammation, trauma, or surgery, and less often a stone or tumor. Acute disease is usually unilateral with pain and erythematous swelling below the medial canthus and purulent reflux; chronic obstruction may present mainly with epiphora, recurrent discharge, or milder swelling. Watering alone is not dacryocystitis and can instead reflect ocular-surface irritation, allergy, eyelid malposition, or excess tear production; this diagnosis requires inflamed or infected lacrimal-sac disease. Spread into the eyelid or orbit, proptosis, painful or restricted eye movement, reduced vision, fever, or systemic toxicity suggests preseptal or orbital cellulitis, abscess, or sepsis and requires urgent treatment rather than delay with local adjunctive care.
